name: Rounding & estimation
description: Rounding to decimal places and significant figures, and estimating calculations.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.

options.text: The zeros in 0.045 are significant figures

questions.explanation: Significant figures start at the first non-zero digit, so the 4 in 0.045 is the first significant figure and the leading zeros only hold the place. 0.512 is much nearer 0.5 than 1, so it does not round up to 1. For 4,753 to 2 significant figures, round the 7 up to 8 in the hundreds, giving 4,800; 4,750 would be rounding to the nearest ten.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.

options.text: The first significant figure of 0.045 is 4
The first significant figure of 0.045 is 0

questions.explanation: Leading zeros sit in front of the first non-zero digit and are only placeholders, so they are never significant. The significant figures of 0.045 are 4 and 5. Rounding 0.0045 to 1 significant figure gives 0.005, not 0.05: the first digit stays in the same column when you round.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.
questions.explanation: A zero after the decimal point and after the first non-zero digit is significant, because it records how precisely the number was measured. So 3.40 has three significant figures (3, 4 and 0) and 0.070 has two (7 and the final 0); the leading zero before the 7 does not count.

The tens digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so the hundreds digit 4 rounds up to 5, giving 3,500. Cutting the number down to 3,400 ignores that. 3,490 is rounded to the nearest ten. Rounding all the way up to 4,000 goes one place too far.

The second decimal digit is 1, which is less than 5, so the tenths digit stays as it is: 2.4. Rounding up to 2.5 would need a 5 or more in the hundredths. 2.0 throws away the tenths as well, and 2.41 has not been rounded at all.

The first significant figure is the 4 in the tenths column, and the next digit is 5, so it rounds up to give 0.5. Keeping 0.4 would be rounding down. 0.05 changes the column of the first significant figure. 1 would round each part of the number separately and lose the tenths entirely.

questions.prompt: Estimate 39 × 21 by rounding each number to 1 significant figure.
questions.explanation: 39 rounds to 40 and 21 rounds to 20, so the estimate is 40 × 20 = 800. 819 is the exact answer, found by calculating and not estimating at all. 600 would come from rounding 39 down to 30, which is not the nearest ten.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.

options.text: An estimate should be close to the exact answer
To estimate, you work out the exact answer and then round it
An estimate is wrong if it is not the exact answer

questions.explanation: An estimate rounds the numbers first and then works with the easier values, so 298 + 405 becomes 300 + 400 = 700 and 19 × 21 becomes 20 × 20 = 400. It is meant to be close to the exact answer, not equal to it, so it is not wrong merely for being approximate. Working out the exact answer first and rounding afterwards is not estimating. Adding 20 + 20 = 40 replaces the multiplication with an addition.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.
questions.explanation: Decimal places are counted after the point; significant figures are counted from the first non-zero digit. So 2 decimal places gives 3.14, and 2 significant figures gives 3.1. Three significant figures gives 3.14 as well, because the 3, 1 and 4 are the first three significant figures. Rounding to 3 with 2 decimal places has kept the wrong number of places.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.
questions.explanation: Rounding looks at the next digit: 8 rounds 6.78 up to 6.8, and 9 rounds 0.499 up to 0.5 even though the digit before it is small. For 2.05 the next digit is 5, so the tenths digit goes up to give 2.1. Cutting the digits off without looking at the next one gives 6.7, 0.4 and 2.0.

questions.prompt: Which of these numbers does NOT round to 0.3 when rounded to 1 significant figure?
questions.explanation: At 1 significant figure the first digit is the tenths digit. The digits 0.27, 0.34 and 0.25 all round to 0.3: 7 and 5 round the 2 up, and 4 leaves it. 0.35 rounds up to 0.4, because the hundredths digit is 5 and the tenths digit goes up from 3 to 4.

The first two significant figures are 2 and 7. The next digit is 4, which is less than 5, so the 7 stays and the rest become zeros: 27,000. 27,500 is rounded to the nearest hundred and 27,480 is cut off rather than rounded. 28,000 rounds the 7 up even though the next digit is only 4.

questions.prompt: Estimate 612 ÷ 28 by rounding each number to 1 significant figure.
questions.explanation: 612 rounds to 600 and 28 rounds to 30, so the estimate is 600 ÷ 30 = 20. 21 is the exact answer rounded, which is calculating rather than estimating. 200 would come from rounding 28 to 3, which drops a digit.

questions.prompt: A school buys 19 boxes of pencils at £4.90 each. Which is the best estimate of the total cost?
questions.explanation: Round both numbers to 1 significant figure: 19 becomes 20 and £4.90 becomes £5, so the estimate is 20 × £5 = £100. £95 rounds only the price and leaves 19 as it is. £93.10 is the exact total, not an estimate. £120 comes from rounding £4.90 up to £6, which is not the nearest pound.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.

options.text: 4.7 rounded to the nearest whole number is 5
4.7 rounded to the nearest whole number is 4
12.3 rounded to the nearest whole number is 12
12.8 rounded to the nearest whole number is 13
12.8 rounded to the nearest whole number is 12

questions.explanation: To round to the nearest whole number, look at the first decimal digit: 7 rounds 4.7 up to 5, 3 leaves 12.3 as 12, and 8 rounds 12.8 up to 13. Cutting off the decimal part instead gives 4 and 12, which are not the nearest whole numbers. 4.7 does lie between 4 and 5, which is why one of them is the nearest.

questions.prompt: Tick every statement that is true.

options.text: 6.5 rounded to the nearest whole number is 7
6.5 rounded to the nearest whole number is 6

questions.explanation: A digit of 5 rounds up, so 6.5 goes to 7 and 3.49 goes to 3.5 because the 9 rounds the 4 up. Rounding 0.512 to 1 significant figure keeps it in the same size of number — 0.5, not 1. Cutting off the second decimal digit of 3.49 gives 3.4, which is rounding down when the next digit is 9.
